svg.aria-label: ATP synthase in the inner mitochondrial membrane. H+ ions in the intermembrane space, where their concentration is high, flow through the Fo part, between the a subunit (stator) and the ring of c subunits (rotor), into the matrix, where H+ concentration is low. The flow turns the rotor and the attached gamma stalk. A b stalk holds the F1 head still. The turning gamma stalk changes the shape of each beta subunit of the F1 head in turn, so ADP and inorganic phosphate bind, are joined into ATP, and ATP is released. In human mitochondria the rotor has 8 c subunits, so 8 H+ make one turn and 3 ATP; with phosphate transport about 4 H+ are used per ATP.

the turning γ stalk changes the shape of

In human mitochondria the rotor has 8 c subunits: 8 H+ turn it once, and one turn makes 3 ATP. Counting the H+ used to bring
phosphate into the matrix, it takes about 4 H+ per ATP.
